titleText.es: Oye, ¿por qué eres TÚ el presidente del Club de la Tautolog... vale, me lo imagino.
titleText.en: Hey, why do YOU get to be the president of Tautology Clu-- wait, I can guess.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to join (a group or organization)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Unirme is the dictionary-form verb unirse with me attached for the speaker. Unirse takes a before the group, organization, or activity being joined.

example.en: I want to join the team.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to show or prove to someone
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Demostrar means ‘to show’ or ‘to prove.’ The attached le marks the person receiving the proof; careful standard Spanish normally uses les when more than one receiver is meant.

example.es: Voy a demostrarle el resultado a Ana.
example.en: I am going to show Ana the result.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: colleagues; peers
honorable; worthy of respect
I belong
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pertenezco is the present form of pertenecer used by the speaker. Pertenecer normally takes a before the group, category, or owner that something belongs to.

example.es: Pertenezco a un club de lectura.
example.en: I belong to a book club.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; required after pertenecer
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use pertenecer a before the group, category, or person that someone or something belongs to. English expresses this a as ‘to.’

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to save myself; to spare myself (time or effort)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ahorrarme joins me to ahorrar. With time, effort, or trouble after it, the form says that the speaker avoids spending or undergoing that amount.

example.es: Quiero ahorrarme una hora de espera.
example.en: I want to save myself an hour of waiting.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: by joining
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Uniéndome is the -iendo action form of unirse with me attached for the speaker. The written accent keeps the original stress after me is added.

example.en: I learned a lot by joining the project.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: club
tautology; a statement that needlessly repeats the same idea
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A tautología says the same thing again in different words or is true simply because of how its terms are defined.

example.es: ‘Entrar dentro’ puede sonar como una tautología.
example.en: ‘Enter inside’ can sound like a tautology.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you found out; you learned (informal singular)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Supiste is the completed-past form of saber used with one familiar listener. In a question about a source, it asks how that person came to know something.

example.en: How did you find out the news?

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks unirse, ‘to join’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Unirse is used with me, te, se, nos, os, or se to match who joins. Se goes before the changed verb when the people joining are ‘they’ or formal ‘you all.’

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they join; you all join (formal)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Unen is the present form used with a plural third-person subject. With se and a, it means that those people join the following group or activity.

example.es: Muchas personas se unen al curso.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: it will have; he or she will have
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tendrá is a future form of tener for one person or thing. Tener changes its stem to tendr- before the future ending -á.

example.en: The building will have another entrance.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Where does me, te, se, nos, or os go when a verb used with one of those words stays in its dictionary form?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Attach the matching small word to the end: unir + me becomes unirme.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A pronominal verb is learned with se, such as unirse or acostarse. When its action verb remains in the unchanged dictionary form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir, replace se with the form that matches the person and write it as part of the same word: acostarme, unirte, or irnos.

example.en: I want to go to bed early.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone joins a group or activity?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of unirse, then a, then name the group or activity.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The small part of unirse changes with the person: me uno, te unes, se une, nos unimos, os unís, or se unen. The word a remains before the group; a plus el contracts to al.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: pertenecer a + grupo, categoría o persona
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something belongs to a group, category, or person?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of pertenecer, then a, then name what it belongs to.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pertenecer changes for the person and time, while a stays before the group, category, or owner. Do not omit a even when English places ‘belong’ directly before another phrase in a different way.

example.es: Estos documentos pertenecen a la biblioteca.
example.en: These documents belong to the library.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone saves themselves time?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of ahorrarse followed by tiempo or a specific amount of time.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The small word changes with the person: me ahorro, te ahorras, se ahorra, nos ahorramos, os ahorráis, or se ahorran. Tiempo names what is saved; other nouns such as esfuerzo or problemas can fill the same role.

example.es: Nos ahorramos tiempo con la lista.
example.en: We save time with the list.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone knows or has heard about a person or thing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of saber followed by de and the person or thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Saber changes for the person and time. De introduces the topic or person known about; depending on context, the expression can mean ‘know about,’ ‘hear about,’ or ‘have news of.’

example.en: Do you know about that project?

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the usual Spanish expression for an honor society?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use sociedad de honor.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is an association that recognizes members for academic achievement or another stated distinction. De honor identifies the type of society; honor stays singular.

example.es: La universidad tiene una sociedad de honor.
example.en: The university has an honor society.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: sociedad de honor · club de la tautología
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why do the honor society and the Tautology Club form the joke?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The honor claim is circular, and the invented club repeatedly states facts that merely repeat themselves.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A tautology repeats the same idea or is true by definition. The club's membership promise says that a group with one million members will have one million members, while its first rule is simply identified as itself. The opening also mocks circular prestige: membership proves someone honorable because honorable people supposedly belong.
